clue.text: Incorporate the sailor's sphere

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is the usual crossword sailor; with the possessive it gives AB'S
an orb is a globe or sphere

explanation.surface: A navy man's globe is being taken over by someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To take in and make part of a whole is both to incorporate and to soak up.

clue.text: Support a cause and marry

definitions.meaning: to champion or adopt a belief or movement
to take as a husband or wife

explanation.surface: Someone backs a movement and weds too.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both adopting a cause and taking a spouse in wedlock.

clue.text: Spend a long time asleep camouflaged in the brae

indicators.note: camouflaged means disguised, so the letters of these words are hidden in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Some animal dozes for months, hidden on a Scottish hillside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'camouflaged' turns IN THE BRAE into the answer. A brae is a Scottish hillside.
explanation.definitionFit: Animals that pass the winter in a dormant state are said to sleep it out this way.

clue.text: Throws away the bandages

definitions.meaning: to fling or toss something out
cloth supports hung from the neck to rest an injured arm

explanation.surface: Someone discards the dressings.
explanation.definitionFit: To fling something is to hurl it, and an arm support is a looped bandage; one word serves both.

clue.text: Multitudes of fishes come to the shallow waters

definitions.meaning: large schools of fish swimming together
sandbanks or shallows where the sea is not deep

explanation.surface: Great numbers of fish arrive in the shallows.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both large schools of fish and sandbanks in the sea.

clue.text: Temporarily dispense with a rugby player

definitions.meaning: to lay off workers for a while
the fly-half in rugby union, also called by this name

explanation.surface: A team briefly does without one of its rugby men.
explanation.walkthrough: In rugby union the fly-half is also known by this name; as a phrasal verb it means to lay workers off for a time.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means laying people off for a while, and the noun names the rugby fly-half position.

clue.text: Neat curve of lake

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, so one beast is an ox
a bow is a curved shape

explanation.surface: A tidy bend in the shoreline of a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neat' looks like tidy but is the old word for cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: A crescent-shaped lake cut off from a meandering river takes this name, usually followed by the word lake.

clue.text: Not for heavy drinkers presumably

parts.note: playfully reads a type of beer as something for those who drink only lightly

explanation.surface: Something not meant for hardened boozers.
explanation.definitionFit: A pale, low-strength beer is jokingly cast as a brew unsuited to serious drinkers.

clue.text: William, note, has a way in prison

indicators.note: in places the following pieces inside the name for William

parts.note: Bill is a short form of the name William
St is the abbreviation for street, a way
E is a note of the musical scale

explanation.surface: A man called William, holding a note, finds a route into jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has ... in' puts A and ST inside BILL, then E follows.
explanation.definitionFit: The Paris fortress-jail stormed in 1789 lends its name to any prison.

clue.text: Sack in French station contains rubbish

indicators.note: contains signals that the French station holds the sack inside it

parts.note: gare is the French word for a railway station
a sack is a bag

explanation.surface: A bag at a Paris railway station is full of refuse.
explanation.definitionFit: Waste or trash, the American word for household refuse.

clue.text: Wizard place, one with clean bracing air

parts.note: Oz is the land of the Wizard of Oz

explanation.surface: The Wizard's land offers fresh, invigorating air.
explanation.definitionFit: Seaside air was popularly thought to be rich in this form of oxygen, so it names fresh bracing air.

clue.text: Begin in earnest as one in the basement may have to do

definitions.meaning: to start working seriously on something

definitions.text: one in the basement may have to do
definitions.meaning: read literally, someone downstairs on ... must go down to it

explanation.surface: Getting started properly, as someone working in the cellar must.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means starting serious work; read literally it is descending to one's work below ground.

clue.text: Letter carried by a messenger

indicators.note: carried by signals letters held within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A note borne by a courier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letter' looks like mail the messenger carries, but it is a letter of the alphabet, the name of S.
explanation.definitionFit: The written name of the nineteenth letter of the alphabet.

clue.text: See 11
Household pest I am unfortunately taken in by

indicators.note: taken in by means held inside the insect that follows

parts.note: a fly is a common insect pest

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things gone wrong, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone admits being fooled by a nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' turns I AM into AMI, which 'taken in by' places inside FLY.
explanation.definitionFit: A household is the group of relatives living together under one roof.

clue.text: Speed does not matter whatever may happen

definitions.meaning: read literally, at whatever pace one likes
in any case, regardless

explanation.surface: However fast, it comes to pass regardless.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means in any event, and literally means at whatever speed.

clue.text: One cannot sleep through it

parts.note: describes a condition of wakefulness rather than a noisy event one fails to sleep through

explanation.surface: Something too disturbing to doze through.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a loud noise; the answer is a disorder that keeps one awake.
explanation.definitionFit: A chronic inability to get to sleep is precisely what keeps one awake all night.

clue.text: Draw a piece clothing

definitions.meaning: a game ending level
a neck garment worn with a shirt

explanation.surface: A drawn match and a garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A level result in a game, and a strip of cloth knotted at the collar.

clue.text: An example of how golfers might differ

definitions.meaning: a case in point
split as two words, golfers might vary in the way they stand to the ball

explanation.surface: A case of golfers having different positions.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a case in point, and split up it describes differing in the way one stands at the ball.

clue.text: A short distance behind

parts.note: ft, short for feet, is a measure of distance

explanation.surface: Something is a little way back.
explanation.definitionFit: Nautically it means towards the stern, at the back of a ship.

clue.text: Invisible passage for translation has not been prepared

definitions.meaning: not able to be seen
a text set in an exam to translate without prior preparation

explanation.surface: An exam text that has not been prepared is out of sight.
explanation.walkthrough: A school exam passage given to translate at sight, without preparation, is called this.
explanation.definitionFit: Something not seen or not visible; also a test passage given without sight beforehand.

clue.text: Take advantage of employment

definitions.meaning: to exploit someone or something
the act of making something serve a purpose

explanation.surface: Someone exploits a job.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means exploit; as a noun the application or purpose of something.

clue.text: I will take attendant out to plunder

indicators.note: out signals the attendant sitting outside the other piece

parts.note: a page is a young attendant
contracted, I will becomes I'll

explanation.surface: A man takes his servant out on a looting spree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take ... out' has PAGE taking I'LL inside it, so PAGE stays outside.
explanation.definitionFit: To loot or ransack, as an army does when sacking a town.

clue.text: Does no one sit down at a meeting of it?

definitions.text: Does no one sit down at a meeting of it?

parts.words: Does no one sit down at a meeting of it?
parts.note: takes a permanent body literally, as a group whose members never take a seat

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about a gathering where everyone stays on their feet.
explanation.definitionFit: A permanent body of members appointed to deal with ongoing business is jokingly imagined as never sitting.

clue.text: Sent in from this game

indicators.note: from signals that the answer is formed out of these letters, rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is dispatched from the court in a sport.
explanation.definitionFit: A racket sport played over a net on a court.

clue.text: Get Ray somehow to move round

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters are got into shape by some unspecified means

explanation.surface: Persuade a man named Ray to turn around.
explanation.definitionFit: To revolve or spin around in circles.

clue.text: See 23
Island mother left with little gratitude

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for mother
ta is a brief, informal thank you

explanation.surface: Mother departed with scant thanks for her island.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is British slang for thank you.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mediterranean island nation south of Sicily.

clue.text: Liner, Queen Elizabeth II

definitions.meaning: something used to draw straight lines
a monarch, one who reigns

explanation.surface: A famous ocean ship named after the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the liner QE2; in fact a liner is a thing for drawing lines, and the Queen was a sovereign.
explanation.definitionFit: A straight-edge draws lines, and a monarch reigns over a country.

clue.text: Well, sort of, Heather has a suspicion

parts.note: an inkwell is a sort of well, so its contents are ink
ling is a type of heather

explanation.surface: A woman called Heather vaguely suspects something.
explanation.definitionFit: A faint notion or slight hint of knowledge.

clue.text: Stay put as cannot stand being drunk

parts.note: one who cannot stand must sit
tight is slang for drunk

explanation.surface: Someone too drunk to stand stays where they are.
explanation.definitionFit: To remain where one is and not move or act.

clue.text: One is in position in a large building

indicators.note: is in signals the one going inside the position

parts.note: a place is a position
A means one

explanation.surface: Someone holds a post in a grand building.
explanation.definitionFit: A royal residence or other grand stately building.
